notes: Frame this as the rare lever that works across crop systems, not a niche technology play. Walk left to right: Gujarat is already a national leader, yet the penetration gap to the top state shows headroom still matters.
title: Micro-irrigation remains Gujarat’s clearest cross-cutting farm lever because adoption is high, scalable, and still trails the national leader
subtitle: This matters because the same intervention improves three constraints at once: it reduces water intensity in stressed districts, raises input-use efficiency through more precise application, and supports higher-value cropping where margins depend on reliable irrigation rather than acreage expansion.

chart.annotation: Gujarat already ranks among India’s leaders, but the gap to Andhra Pradesh shows material room to scale a proven resilience and efficiency lever.
chart.source: Source: PMKSY Per Drop More Crop, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2024 [[src:official]]

insights.text: **Gujarat** has **11.2 lakh ha**[[src:official]] under micro-irrigation, placing it behind only **Andhra Pradesh** at **17.7 lakh ha**[[src:official]] in this peer set and well ahead of **Karnataka** at **9.3 lakh ha**[[src:official]], which shows the state is already operating from meaningful installed scale rather than pilot-level adoption.

The ranking matters because this is one of the few levers that travels across farm systems. Gujarat’s **11.2 lakh ha**[[src:official]] exceeds **Maharashtra** at **8.7 lakh ha**[[src:official]] and **Tamil Nadu** at **6.1 lakh ha**[[src:official]], supporting the case that irrigation efficiency can cut water pressure while strengthening crop economics in both field-crop and horticulture belts.

Headroom remains material. The gap between **Andhra Pradesh** at **17.7 lakh ha**[[src:official]] and **Gujarat** at **11.2 lakh ha**[[src:official]] is large enough to justify execution-focused expansion through drip, sprinkler, fertigation, and tighter on-farm water management rather than relying on new acreage or broad untargeted subsidy expansion.

footnote: Peer-state comparison is shown as evidence that micro-irrigation is already proven at scale in Gujarat yet still has meaningful room to expand as a resilience, efficiency, and value-capture lever. Source: PMKSY Per Drop More Crop, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2024 [[src:official]]
